title: Generosity at work
tomorrow: dad's back Monday and wants double shifts. who tells him to stop?

segments.voice: Yesterday, avoiding interest: an old loan, and a way out taken step by step. Today the money stays in the drawer. What gets given is time.

Five minutes past the end of a shift. Coat on, keys out, and the line at the register runs to the door. A coworker looks up, and the look says everything. Most jobs have that moment. Here's an older one. Medina, a cold morning, an army on its way. The city has decided to dig a trench across the open ground, and everyone has a stretch of it. Down in the dirt, hauling earth like the rest, is the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. A companion who saw him said the dust covered the skin of his belly.
screen: `FIVE MINUTES PAST THE SHIFT.` → `A COLD MORNING, A TRENCH.` → `DUST ON THE PROPHET.`

segments.voice: He could have stood on the rim and pointed. He didn't. Anas, who was there, remembered people digging with their own hands, with no one to do it for them. And the Prophet called out a line of verse over the shovels, a prayer for the diggers: the real life is the life to come, so forgive the helpers and the emigrants. The diggers sang back, promising to keep at it. A call, and an answer, while the dirt flew. That's generosity at work. Not a bonus. Shoulders, time, showing up in someone else's stretch of the trench. The Qur'an says it in Pickthall's words: "help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty." A hadith in Sahih Muslim turns it into a promise: God is in the help of His servant as long as the servant is in the help of his brother. Notice which way that runs. You take half a coworker's line, or untangle their report, and the report says God is helping you while you do it. Another hadith counts even lifting someone's bags onto their ride as charity. One to tell a friend tonight: what the diggers remembered about the leader of their city was the dust on him, not a speech.
screen: `NO ONE TO DIG FOR THEM.` · `A CALL, AND THE DIGGERS' ANSWER.` · `HELP ONE ANOTHER.` · `GOD HELPS WHILE YOU HELP.` · then, large: `GENEROUS AT WORK.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person you work or study beside who is carrying a heavy stretch right now. Send them one small, specific offer: I can close tonight, I can read your draft. If you pray, you can ask that the help lands well, then sit quietly until the time is up.
screen: `ONE PERSON, ONE HEAVY STRETCH.` · `ONE SMALL, SPECIFIC OFFER.`

segments.voice: Generosity at work: giving time and shoulders, not only money, to the people beside you. At the trench, the Prophet carried the earth too.
Your line: generous at work, the way he carried earth at the trench. The shift isn't over until the line is.

chat.meaning: At the trench the Prophet carried earth himself, and a hadith says God helps His servant while the servant helps another.

Medina.meaning: the city where the Prophet lived his last years

Anas.meaning: Anas ibn Malik, a companion who served the Prophet

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a major collection of reports of the Prophet's words and deeds

Pickthall.meaning: Marmaduke Pickthall, who translated the Qur'an into English

sources.quoted: help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2834 (Anas: a cold morning at the trench, people digging with no one to do it for them; the Prophet's verse for the Ansar and Muhajirun and their answer)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4106 (al-Bara': he carried earth on the day of the trench until the dust covered the skin of his belly)
Sahih Muslim 2699 (God is in the help of His servant as long as the servant is in the help of his brother)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2989 (helping a man onto his mount or lifting his belongings onto it is charity)

notes: Confirm the exact Pickthall wording of the 5:2 phrase.

Bukhari 2834, 4106 (also 2835-2837, 4099-4104) and 2989, Muslim 2699: confirm numbering and that the paraphrases are fair. 'A cold morning' and 'no one to do it for them' are from Anas's report; 'an army on its way' is the setting of the Battle of the Trench (al-Ahzab).

The verse the Prophet called out is paraphrased (the life of the hereafter is the real life; forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirun); the diggers' answer is paraphrased as a promise to keep at it (in the report, a pledge to Muhammad to keep striving).
